newsitem.title: USA: Microsoft to launch multimedia platform.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft to launch multimedia platform.

text.p: Microsoft Corp on Monday plans to announce a platform for delivering multimedia content such as audio and video over corporate networks and the Internet, company executives said.

Microsoft NetShow, a component of the Windows NT and Windows 95 operating system, will be available in a test version immediately and will be finalized by the end of the year, said Nevet Basker, a Microsoft group product manager.
At first the technology is expected to be used to distribute audio and graphics through corporate "intranets," or private computer networks that follow Internet protocols.

Ultimately NetShow could be used to boost the performance of live video presentations over the Internet, currently impractical because most users receive data at speeds much slower than necessary for true video performance.

The new platform, which will be freely available over the Internet, is based on Microsoft's video server, a project code-named Tiger that was developed for interactive television but is still in the testing stage.
Basker said the new technology, which allows users to receive data "streams" with only a short delay, could be used for corporate training presentations or reference materials enhanced by audio.
A possible application would be what the company calls "illustrated audio," which might consist of slides from a presentation along with an audio narrative.
Several dozen software companies have signed up to provide products that build on the new platform, which will be announced at an industry conference in Atlanta.
Dwight Davis, editor of Windows Watcher, an industry newsletter, said that so far there were few applications for the new platform.
"Three or four years down the road this kind of capability will be commonplace, and people will be using it for things that most of us can't foresee right now," he said.
